content:
Morning!  Real tongue twister traditional Irish song here for you today!

[tab][ch]G[/ch]                           [ch]C[/ch]              [ch]G[/ch]
I am a little beggarman and begging I have been[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                               [ch]F[/ch]
For three score or more in this little isle of green[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                         [ch]C[/ch]       [ch]G[/ch]
I'm known from the Liffey down to Segue[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                            [ch]D[/ch]          [ch]G[/ch]
And I'm known by the name of old Johnny Dhu[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                                     [ch]C[/ch]              [ch]G[/ch]
Of all the trade's that's going, sure begging is the best[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                               [ch]F[/ch]
For when a man is tired, he can sit down and rest[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                                 [ch]C[/ch]               [ch]G[/ch]
He can beg for his dinner, he has nothing else to do[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                                   [ch]D[/ch]         [ch]G[/ch]
Only cut around the corner with his old rig-a-doo[/tab]



[tab][ch]F[/ch]                         [ch]C[/ch]
I slept in the barn, down at Caurabawn[/tab]
[tab]  [ch]G[/ch]                       [ch]F[/ch]
A wet night came on and I slept 'till the dawn[/tab]
[tab]     [ch]G[/ch]                         [ch]C[/ch]           [ch]G[/ch]
With holes in the roof and the rain coming through[/tab]
[tab]        [ch]G[/ch]                            [ch]D[/ch]              [ch]G[/ch]
And the rats and the cats, they were playing peek-a-boo[/tab]
[tab][ch]F[/ch]                            [ch]C[/ch]
When who did I waken but the woman of the house[/tab]
[tab]         [ch]G[/ch]                          [ch]F[/ch]
With her white spotty apron and her calico blouse[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                         [ch]C[/ch]       [ch]G[/ch]
She began to frighten and I said "boo[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                               [ch]D[/ch]           [ch]G[/ch]
Aarah, don't be afraid mam it's only Johnny Dhu"[/tab]



[tab][ch]G[/ch]                           [ch]C[/ch]        [ch]G[/ch]
I met a little flaxy-haired girl one day[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                                 [ch]F[/ch]
"Good morning little flaxy-haired girl" I did say[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                                 [ch]C[/ch]          [ch]G[/ch]
"Good morning little beggarman, a how do you do[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                                    [ch]D[/ch]         [ch]G[/ch]
With your rags and you tags and your old rig-a-doo"[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                              [ch]C[/ch]            [ch]G[/ch]
I'll buy a pair of leggings, a collar and a tie[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                          [ch]F[/ch]
And a nice young lady I'll fetch by and by[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                                   [ch]C[/ch]           [ch]G[/ch]
I'll buy a pair of goggles and I'll colour them blue[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                                [ch]D[/ch]        [ch]G[/ch]
And an old fashioned lady I will make her too[/tab]



[tab][ch]F[/ch]                     [ch]C[/ch]
Over the road with my pack on my back[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                       [ch]F[/ch]
Over the fields with my great heavy sack[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                             [ch]C[/ch]            [ch]G[/ch]
With holes in my shoes and my toes peeping through[/tab]
[tab][ch]G[/ch]                                     [ch]D[/ch]          [ch]G[/ch]
Singing skinny-me-rink a doodle o and old Johnny Dhu[/tab]
[tab][ch]F[/ch]                               [ch]C[/ch]
I must be going to bed for it's getting late at night[/tab]
[tab]    [ch]G[/ch]                    [ch]F[/ch]
The fire's all raked and out goes the light[/tab]
[tab]   [ch]G[/ch]                                [ch]C[/ch]         [ch]G[/ch]
So now you've heard the story of my old rig-a-doo[/tab]
[tab]     [ch]G[/ch]                                 [ch]D[/ch]          [ch]G[/ch]
It's good-bye and God be with you says old Johnny Dhu[/tab]
